jobs.title: Director Data, AI, and Specialized Business
jobs.description:
Job Description

What is the Opportunity?

This is an opportunity to lead the Data, AI, KYC and Specialized Business portfolio within RBC Caribbean Banking Technology, a team dedicated to delivering modern, resilient solutions for our Caribbean businesses and clients. We are all in on Agile delivery, DevOps, open source, cloud and modern engineering practices, and the work is highly visible: our applications are used daily by RBC staff and clients across the region.

Reporting to the Senior Director, the Director owns three connected mandates. First, the modernization of the Caribbean data foundation: evolving the data lake, data architecture and data products so that the business can trust and use its data. Second, AI engineering: building and operating production grade AI solutions for clients and colleagues, from generative and agentic AI to intelligent automation, with responsible AI and regulatory controls built in. Third, software development and delivery for KYC and Specialized Business Applications: leading the engineering team accountable for a portfolio of vendor applications and for active development of the KYC platform, and delivering the associated project portfolio on time and with quality.

The successful candidate combines hands on technical credibility in data and AI engineering with proven project delivery, vendor management and people leadership, and a clear understanding of the banking industry’s data, processes and regulatory obligations. They are comfortable navigating ambiguity and leading in a fast paced, rapidly evolving technology environment.

What Will You Do?

Data modernization and data foundation

Own end to end delivery of data engineering and data product initiatives for the Caribbean, working closely with business and technology stakeholders to define scope, priorities and expectations.
Lead the data modernization roadmap and architecture, retire legacy data flows, and establish the platform as the standard foundation for analytics, reporting, consolidation of siloed data, removal of duplicated data profiles, and AI solutions.
Establish and enforce data governance practices (data dictionary, lineage, quality and access controls) that meet regulatory and audit expectations across Caribbean jurisdictions.
Mature CI/CD and orchestration for data pipelines, with automated testing, monitoring and service level objectives for production data.
Partner with business lines to define data products and self service capabilities that create measurable value.

AI engineering and AI solutions

Define, communicate and execute the AI solutions roadmap for Caribbean applications, aligned to the business vision and to emerging AI capabilities (generative AI, agentic AI, large language models, intelligent process automation).
Build and grow an AI engineering practice: design, develop, deploy and operate production ready AI solutions for clients and colleagues, well integrated with existing Caribbean systems and data infrastructure.
Establish the engineering foundations for AI at scale: reusable patterns for LLM integration, retrieval augmented generation (RAG), agent orchestration, evaluation and testing frameworks, prompt and context management, and an AI asset registry with versioning.
Lead operational support for AI solutions in production: monitoring and observability, incident management, logging, performance tuning, drift and quality detection, and AIOps.
Champion ethical and responsible AI: ensure all initiatives comply with RBC policies and regulatory requirements applicable to banking in Canada and the Caribbean (e.g., OSFI guidance, model risk management, privacy legislation), and partner with Risk, Compliance and Legal on approvals.
Stay abreast of AI advancements, evaluate their applicability to the Caribbean banking context, and act as an internal thought leader on applied AI.

Software development and delivery: KYC and Specialized Business Applications

Lead the software development team accountable for a portfolio of vendor applications supporting Specialized Business functions, including release management, configuration, integration, upgrades, incident response and production support.
Lead active development of the KYC platform: own the backlog, architecture direction, engineering quality, security and delivery cadence, in close partnership with AML/Compliance and Operations stakeholders.
Manage vendor relationships and service ownership: contracts and SLAs, roadmap alignment, escalations and performance reviews.
Deliver the project portfolio through disciplined Agile delivery (planning, dependency and risk management, status reporting and executive communication) with accountability for scope, schedule, budget and quality.
Embed modern engineering practices (DevOps, automation, CI/CD, automated testing) to improve resilience, reduce operational risk and cost, and strengthen security and availability.
Ensure disaster recovery, uptime and resilience for all production systems in the portfolio.

Leadership and stakeholder engagement

Lead, mentor and grow a high performing, cross regional team of data engineers, AI engineers and software developers across Toronto and the Caribbean, fostering technical excellence, collaboration and continuous improvement.
Own talent acquisition, performance management, career development and retention for the team.
Collaborate with Caribbean business leaders, product managers and technology partners to understand requirements, define scope and manage expectations; communicate clearly at senior levels.
Contribute to the Senior Director’s broader technology strategy and represent the portfolio in governance forums.

What do you need to succeed?

Must hav
e

10+ years of progressive experience across data engineering, software development and/or AI engineering, with 8+ years in a leadership role managing engineers and delivery teams, with a strong emphasis on production delivery and operations.
Proven experience working within the banking or financial services industry, with a clear understanding of its data, processes, regulatory context and business challenges.
Demonstrated track record of delivering large scale, multi project programs in complex enterprise environments, including Agile delivery, dependency mitigation, budget and vendor management.
Hands on AI engineering skills and proven experience building AI solutions from concept to production: LLM integration, RAG, agent frameworks, evaluation and testing, and AI observability.

jobs.title: Vice President Finance
jobs.description:
GlassRatner Executive Search is partnering with eTracks Tire Management Systems (eTracks) to appoint its next Vice President, Finance.

eTracks is a leading Producer Responsibility Organization (PRO) responsible for managing tire recycling programs on behalf of tire producers across Ontario. Established in 2017 under the Canada Not-for-Profit Corporations Act, the company was created by the Tire and Rubber Association of Canada (TRAC) to support compliance with Ontario's Resource Recovery and Circular Economy Act (RRCEA).

Today, eTracks plays a critical role in advancing Ontario's circular economy by overseeing the collection, transportation, and recycling of used tires through a network of service providers. As a mission-driven organization, eTracks combines the purpose of a not-for-profit with the complexity and scale of a commercial enterprise.

As the organization enters its next phase of transformation, eTracks is seeking a strategic, forward-thinking Vice President, Finance to join its Senior Leadership Team.

The Mandate

The Vice President, Finance will serve as a strategic partner to the CEO and Senior Leadership Team, ensuring the organization has the financial insight, discipline, and operational support necessary to achieve its long-term objectives. Building on a strong financial foundation, the VP, Finance will help drive organizational performance, strengthen decision-making through data and analytics, support key strategic initiatives, and enhance overall business effectiveness.

This role is ideal for a finance leader who combines financial rigour with commercial acumen, an operational mindset, and the ability to navigate a complex stakeholder community in a highly regulated industry.

The Opportunity

Reporting directly to the CEO, the Vice President, Finance will serve as the organization's senior financial leader and a trusted advisor on strategic, operational, and financial matters. This role offers the opportunity to contribute well beyond traditional finance leadership, helping shape organizational strategy, evaluate business opportunities, support long term growth initiatives, and improve overall organizational performance.

The successful candidate will work closely with the CEO, Board of Directors, and Finance, Audit and Investment Committee (FAIC), providing financial leadership, business insight, and sound judgment across the organization.

The VP, Finance will oversee all aspects of financial management, including financial planning and analysis, budgeting, forecasting, reporting, treasury, risk management, governance, and
compliance. They will play a key role in enhancing management reporting and business intelligence capabilities, supporting technology and systems initiatives, and driving continuous improvement across financial and operational processes. In addition, the VP, Finance will lead and develop the finance team, fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and high performance.

To be considered for the role, you will possess the following:

University degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, or a related discipline
CPA designation required
10 years of experience in senior-level finance or accounting leadership roles
Track record as the senior finance executive within a small-to-mid-sized organization, both in a hands-on and strategic capacity
Experience from supply chain and logistics industry, waste management, environmental services or process manufacturing ideal
Experience operating within regulated environments highly preferred
Demonstrated success partnering directly with a CEO and Board of Directors
Team management and leadership, coaching, developing and mentoring a high performing team
Deep expertise in financial planning, forecasting, budgeting, reporting, internal controls, and business analysis
Experience leading ERP implementations, systems optimization initiatives, technology-enabled transformations, or major change projects enterprise-wide
Exceptional levels of integrity, diplomacy, strong negotiation skills, accountability and delivery mindset

This is an opportunity to play a key leadership role in a respected organization at the intersection of sustainability, business services, and public policy at the forefront of the circular economy. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to influence strategy, identify opportunities for continuous improvements and drive transformation initiatives, and help shape the future of an organization making a meaningful environmental impact across Ontario.

jobs.title: Vice President, Finance
jobs.description:
Who we are

Kilmer Group is a multi-generational platform for business development and investment, built on operational excellence, long-term stewardship, and trusted relationships. Headquartered in Toronto, we invest across three core sectors: Private Equity, Infrastructure & Real Estate, and Sports & Media, partnering with exceptional management teams to build and grow enduring businesses.

Kilmer Group has built a reputation for disciplined investment, active ownership, and creating long-term value. Our approach is grounded in partnership, integrity, and a commitment to building businesses that generate lasting impact for our partners, stakeholders, and the communities we serve.

Who we need

Reporting to the CFO, we are hiring a Vice President, Finance to play a key leadership role across Kilmer Group's finance function. As our new Vice President, Finance, you will combine financial stewardship with strategic partnership, helping guide decisions that support the continued growth and evolution of a diversified investment platform. Working closely with the CFO, senior leaders, and investment teams, you will oversee financial reporting, treasury, budgeting, investment portfolio reporting, and governance while providing the financial insight that supports investment decisions, business performance, and long-term value creation. You will lead a finance team and contribute across a broad range of initiatives, from evaluating acquisitions and investments to strengthening reporting, improving processes, and building the financial capabilities and infrastructure needed to support the organization's continued growth.

This is an existing, full-time opportunity based in the Toronto office, working onsite five days per week.

What’s in it for you?

Strategic influence. Reporting directly to the CFO, you will act as a trusted partner to the executive leadership team, contributing financial insight that informs investment decisions, capital allocation, and the long-term direction of Kilmer Group.

Breadth and exposure. This is an opportunity to apply your expertise across a diverse investment portfolio rather than within a single operating business. You will work on initiatives spanning financial reporting, tax, budgeting, long-term forecasting, governance, and business performance.

Build what's next. Technology and AI are transforming the finance function, and Kilmer Group is evolving with it - strengthening reporting, deepening financial analysis, and modernizing our processes to harness these new tools. You will help build new capabilities, grow a high-performing team, and shape a financial foundation built for long-term success.

As our new VP Finance, you will

Lead the finance function.
You will oversee accounting, treasury, financial reporting, and cash management across a complex, multi-entity organization, ensuring strong controls, effective budgeting, and timely, accurate reporting. As a trusted partner to the CFO, you will provide the financial leadership and operational oversight that enables the team to deliver with confidence while supporting the organization's growth objectives.
Provide strategic financial insight.
You will translate financial information into meaningful analysis that supports executive decision-making. Working closely with the CFO and senior leaders, you will develop reporting and insights that strengthen planning, support investment decisions, and provide a clearer understanding of business performance across the organization.
Support investments and corporate growth.
You will partner with the investment team on acquisitions, portfolio reporting, valuations, due diligence, and other strategic initiatives. You will work closely with leaders across Kilmer Group and its portfolio companies, providing financial guidance and building trusted relationships that support long-term value creation.
Lead and develop the team.
You will mentor, coach, and support the continued growth of the finance team while fostering a collaborative, accountable, and low-ego environment. You will build capability and create opportunities for continuous learning amongst the team.

You bring

The leadership.
You have experience leading high-performing finance teams and fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement. You are a trusted advisor who can balance strategic priorities with operational execution while building strong relationships across the organization.
The foundation.
You are a CPA, CA with experience gained in both public accounting and industry, ideally including a Big 4 audit environment. You bring strong technical knowledge of ASPE and IFRS, investment holding company accounting, including asset valuations and investee reporting. You have experience with compliance and risk to ensure adherence with tax laws, accounting standards and internal controls. You know how to apply this technical foundation in a commercial environment, combining accounting expertise with sound strategic and business judgment.
The financial expertise.
You bring experience across financial reporting, treasury, budgeting, cash management, tax and corporate governance within complex organizations. You have worked with investment portfolios, valuations, transactions, or corporate development activities and are comfortable partnering with senior leaders to support investment decisions and long-term value creation.
The analytical mindset.
You are naturally curious and continuously look for ways to improve how work gets done. You leverage data and technology to strengthen reporting and decision-making, and you are excited by the opportunity to modernize finance through automation and the thoughtful application of AI.
The communication skills.
You can translate complex financial information into clear recommendations that support decision-making. Whether working with executives, portfolio company leaders, auditors, or external advisors, you build credibility through sound judgment, strong communication, and a collaborative approach.

Why join Kilmer Group?

Today, Kilmer Group continues to build on decades of successful investment and business leadership offering a dynamic and supportive environment with opportunities for growth and development. Beyond our investments, we are committed to strengthening the communities where we live and work through initiatives that support sport, health, research, and community development. Joining Kilmer Group means becoming part of an organization that thinks for the long term, values partnership, and is committed to building a lasting legacy.

Join us

We recognize that no candidate brings every qualification to a role. If your experience is closely aligned with what we are looking for and you are excited by the opportunity to contribute to Kilmer Group, we encourage you to apply. We look forward to learning more about your experience and the perspective you would bring to our team.

What you can expect from our interview process

A virtual interview with a Talent Advisor to discuss your interest in joining Kilmer Group and your experience. The conversation will be recorded using BrightHire, an AI-powered video interview tool. More details will be shared when you are invited to interview.
An in-person conversation with the Chief Financial Officer to discuss your leadership experience, your approach to building high-performing finance functions, and how you partner with executives to support investment decisions and long-term growth.
An in-person presentation and discussion with the Vice President, Talent and Special Projects and a senior member of the finance team. You will be asked to prepare and present a case study, followed by a conversation about your thinking, priorities, and leadership approach.
A final in-person conversation with the Chief Financial Officer to explore mutual fit, discuss your vision for the role, and answer any remaining questions. Finalists may also have the opportunity to meet additional members of the leadership team.

Kilmer Group is committed to creating a workplace where people are treated with respect, supported in their development, and empowered to contribute their best work. We recognize that diverse perspectives strengthen our business and help us make better decisions for our organization, our partners, and the communities in which we operate.

We welcome applications from all qualified candidates and are committed to providing an accessible recruitment process. If you require accommodation at any stage of the recruitment process, please let us know and we will work with you to meet your needs.

Position Purpose The Chief Transformation Officer (CTO) is a senior leadership role responsible for leading Lifesaving Society Canada’s transformation agenda and converting strategic priorities into sustainable national operating capabilities. The CTO will oversee VITA (CRM), artificial intelligence, the digital landscape and training manuals, virtual training, and related transformation initiatives. The position reports to the CEO, operates with significant delegated authority, manages related budgets and vendors, and works across the Board of Directors, Management Team, Branches, committees and external partners.
Leadership Mandate • Provide enterprise-wide leadership for LSC transformation initiatives, ensuring projects are coordinated, prioritized, resourced and aligned with LSC’s strategic direction, programs and delivery models.
•  Act independently within approved authority, escalating matters to the CEO or Board when they involve material strategic, financial, policy, privacy, security or reputational implications.
• Translate transformation strategy into clear roadmaps, implementation plans, governance structures, budgets, milestones, accountabilities and measurable outcomes.
•  Serve as a bridge between national strategy and practical implementation across the National Office and provincial Branches.

Key Accountabilities 1.  Transformation Strategy and Portfolio Leadership • Lead and coordinate LSC’s transformation portfolio, including VITA, AI, development, digital-resource modernization and virtual training.
• Establish integrated roadmaps, priorities, dependencies, milestones, risk controls and performance measures across transformation initiatives to include the subscription model.
• Identify opportunities to improve service delivery, operational efficiency, user experience, scalability, national consistency and revenue sustainability.
• Prepare recommendations, business cases and decision materials for the CEO, Management Team, Board and committees.
• Ensure transformation work reflects LSC’s national structure, Branch realities, program standards and delivery model.
2.  VITA (CRM) Platform Leadership • Provide national operational ownership and product coordination for VITA through implementation, stabilization and ongoing evolution.
• Manage the VITA scope baseline, roadmap, backlog, release calendar, gap register and national decision log.

• Maintain disciplined national change management for requests affecting shared data, workflows, permissions, reporting, integrations, configuration, scope and cross-Branch operations.
• Coordinate data governance and reporting, including data definitions, controlled values, data-quality measures, duplicate-management rules, reporting definitions and dashboard-access governance.
• Oversee VITA policies, business rules, user guides, role-based training materials, Branch toolkits, job aids, FAQs, release communications and other adoption resources.
• Ensure access and permissions are governed through an approved role-permission model, appropriate authorization, periodic review and segregation-of-duties controls; the CTO is accountable for business governance of access, not unrestricted technical control by a single individual.
• Coordinate privacy, security and compliance processes with the designated privacy/compliance resource and ensure risks are appropriately identified and escalated.
• Develop costed recommendations for post-implementation enhancements, support, staffing, funding and the long-term role of VITA in LSC’s digital architecture.
3.  Artificial Intelligence • Develop and lead an LSC approach to responsible AI adoption that supports operations, program delivery, service quality and organizational capacity.
• Identify, assess and prioritize practical AI use cases, including opportunities to streamline work, improve knowledge access and support decision-making.
• Establish appropriate governance, risk, privacy, security, human oversight and change-management practices for AI use.
• Build organizational AI literacy through guidance, training and practical support for staff and volunteers.
• Monitor emerging AI capabilities and recommend investments, pilots and policies appropriate to LSC.
5.  Digital Landscape and Training Resources • Lead the development of an integrated digital landscape for access to LSC resources and manuals.
• Oversee approaches to digital access, permissions, security, fees, version control and distribution of training and operational resources.
• Work with program leaders and Branches to ensure digital resources are current, accessible, practical and aligned with national standards.
• Identify opportunities to reduce duplication and improve the discoverability and management of national digital content.
6.  Virtual Training and Online Learning • Lead the development and expansion of virtual training and future online course offerings.
• Coordinate platform requirements, online registration, fee models, learner experience, training resources and operational support.
7.  Governance, Stakeholder and Change Leadership • Work   directly   with    the   CEO,  Board   of    Directors,   Management  Team,  Branches, commissions/committees and project groups on transformation priorities.
• Prepare clear reports, recommendations, dashboards, risk updates and decision materials for governance and management audiences.
• Maintain appropriate governance artifacts, including RACI/accountability frameworks, risk and issue registers, change logs, decision logs, policies, SOPs and project records.
• Lead organizational change, communications, training and adoption activities so that new systems and operating models are understood and used effectively.
• Build strong working relationships across LSC while respecting Branch operational responsibilities and national standards.
8.  Financial, Vendor and Resource Management • Develop and manage budgets for the transformation portfolio and its component initiatives.
• Monitor expenditures, forecasts, contracts and financial performance; identify variances and recommend corrective action.
• Lead procurement and vendor/service-provider relationships within delegated authority, with clear deliverables, service expectations and accountability.
• Assess resource and staffing requirements and recommend sustainable operating models for transformation functions.
• Ensure projects have realistic costs, timelines, ownership, risk controls and measures of success.

Qualifications and Experience • Progressive leadership experience in organizational transformation, digital modernization, technology-enabled service delivery, operations or a related field.
• Experience leading complex cross-functional initiatives involving multiple stakeholders, competing priorities and organizational change.
• Experience with CRM or enterprise platforms, vendor management, implementation, stabilization and continuous improvement.

• Experience working with senior management, boards, committees and governance processes.

• Knowledge of French, both written and spoken, is an asset.

Today, eTracks plays a critical role in advancing Ontario's circular economy by overseeing the collection, transportation, and recycling of used tires through a network of service providers. As a mission-driven organization, eTracks combines the purpose of a not-for-profit with the complexity and scale of a commercial enterprise.

The Vice President, Finance will serve as a strategic partner to the CEO and Senior Leadership Team, ensuring the organization has the financial insight, discipline, and operational support necessary to achieve its long-term objectives. Kilmer Group is a multi-generational platform for business development and investment, built on operational excellence, long-term stewardship, and trusted relationships. Kilmer Group has built a reputation for disciplined investment, active ownership, and creating long-term value. Our approach is grounded in partnership, integrity, and a commitment to building businesses that generate lasting impact for our partners, stakeholders, and the communities we serve.

Who we need

Reporting to the CFO, we are hiring a Vice President, Finance to play a key leadership role across Kilmer Group's finance function. As our new Vice President, Finance, you will combine financial stewardship with strategic partnership, helping guide decisions that support the continued growth and evolution of a diversified investment platform. Working closely with the CFO, senior leaders, and investment teams, you will oversee financial reporting, treasury, budgeting, investment portfolio reporting, and governance while providing the financial insight that supports investment decisions, business performance, and long-term value creation. You will lead a finance team and contribute across a broad range of initiatives, from evaluating acquisitions and investments to strengthening reporting, improving processes, and building the financial capabilities and infrastructure needed to support the organization's continued growth.

This is an existing, full-time opportunity based in the Toronto office, working onsite five days per week.

What’s in it for you?

Strategic influence. Reporting directly to the CFO, you will act as a trusted partner to the executive leadership team, contributing financial insight that informs investment decisions, capital allocation, and the long-term direction of Kilmer Group.

Breadth and exposure. This is an opportunity to apply your expertise across a diverse investment portfolio rather than within a single operating business. You will work on initiatives spanning financial reporting, tax, budgeting, long-term forecasting, governance, and business performance.

Build what's next. Technology and AI are transforming the finance function, and Kilmer Group is evolving with it - strengthening reporting, deepening financial analysis, and modernizing our processes to harness these new tools. You will help build new capabilities, grow a high-performing team, and shape a financial foundation built for long-term success.

As our new VP Finance, you will

Lead the finance function.
You will oversee accounting, treasury, financial reporting, and cash management across a complex, multi-entity organization, ensuring strong controls, effective budgeting, and timely, accurate reporting. As a trusted partner to the CFO, you will provide the financial leadership and operational oversight that enables the team to deliver with confidence while supporting the organization's growth objectives.
Provide strategic financial insight.
You will translate financial information into meaningful analysis that supports executive decision-making. Working closely with the CFO and senior leaders, you will develop reporting and insights that strengthen planning, support investment decisions, and provide a clearer understanding of business performance across the organization.
Support investments and corporate growth.
You will partner with the investment team on acquisitions, portfolio reporting, valuations, due diligence, and other strategic initiatives. You will work closely with leaders across Kilmer Group and its portfolio companies, providing financial guidance and building trusted relationships that support long-term value creation.
Lead and develop the team.
You will mentor, coach, and support the continued growth of the finance team while fostering a collaborative, accountable, and low-ego environment. You will build capability and create opportunities for continuous learning amongst the team.

You bring

The leadership.
You have experience leading high-performing finance teams and fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement. You are a trusted advisor who can balance strategic priorities with operational execution while building strong relationships across the organization.
The foundation.
You are a CPA, CA with experience gained in both public accounting and industry, ideally including a Big 4 audit environment. You bring strong technical knowledge of ASPE and IFRS, investment holding company accounting, including asset valuations and investee reporting. You have experience with compliance and risk to ensure adherence with tax laws, accounting standards and internal controls. You know how to apply this technical foundation in a commercial environment, combining accounting expertise with sound strategic and business judgment.
The financial expertise.
You bring experience across financial reporting, treasury, budgeting, cash management, tax and corporate governance within complex organizations. You have worked with investment portfolios, valuations, transactions, or corporate development activities and are comfortable partnering with senior leaders to support investment decisions and long-term value creation.
The analytical mindset.
You are naturally curious and continuously look for ways to improve how work gets done. You leverage data and technology to strengthen reporting and decision-making, and you are excited by the opportunity to modernize finance through automation and the thoughtful application of AI.
The communication skills.
You can translate complex financial information into clear recommendations that support decision-making. Whether working with executives, portfolio company leaders, auditors, or external advisors, you build credibility through sound judgment, strong communication, and a collaborative approach.

Why join Kilmer Group?

Today, Kilmer Group continues to build on decades of successful investment and business leadership offering a dynamic and supportive environment with opportunities for growth and development. Beyond our investments, we are committed to strengthening the communities where we live and work through initiatives that support sport, health, research, and community development. Joining Kilmer Group means becoming part of an organization that thinks for the long term, values partnership, and is committed to building a lasting legacy.

Join us

We recognize that no candidate brings every qualification to a role. If your experience is closely aligned with what we are looking for and you are excited by the opportunity to contribute to Kilmer Group, we encourage you to apply. We look forward to learning more about your experience and the perspective you would bring to our team.

A virtual interview with a Talent Advisor to discuss your interest in joining Kilmer Group and your experience. The conversation will be recorded using BrightHire, an AI-powered video interview tool. More details will be shared when you are invited to interview.
An in-person conversation with the Chief Financial Officer to discuss your leadership experience, your approach to building high-performing finance functions, and how you partner with executives to support investment decisions and long-term growth.
An in-person presentation and discussion with the Vice President, Talent and Special Projects and a senior member of the finance team. You will be asked to prepare and present a case study, followed by a conversation about your thinking, priorities, and leadership approach.

Define enterprise data strategy: Partner with the CIO and senior leaders to establish a multi-year data management and BI strategy aligned with business priorities, technology roadmaps, investment plans, and operational requirements.
Build the data operating model: Establish clear ownership, stewardship, decision rights, architecture standards, delivery practices, and support responsibilities across corporate and regional teams.

Protect sensitive information: Work with cybersecurity, legal, privacy, export compliance, quality, and security teams to ensure data is appropriately classified, protected, accessed, and shared.

Enable self-service analytics: Build governed data products and semantic models that allow business users to access reliable insights without creating uncontrolled copies of sensitive information.
Advance analytics and AI: Identify and govern use cases including predictive maintenance, component reliability, inventory optimization, demand forecasting, anomaly detection, and program risk monitoring, with appropriate ownership, data quality, human oversight, and security controls.

Industry experience: Experience in aerospace, defense, aviation, MRO, or another highly regulated and asset-intensive industry is strongly preferred.
ERP/MRO expertise: Demonstrated experience improving data quality and reporting within complex ERP or MRO environments; experience with Ramco is a significant asset, while comparable aviation or enterprise platforms are also relevant.
International experience: Experience operating across multiple countries, legal entities, or security domains, particularly Canada and the United States, is preferred.
Data expertise: Strong knowledge of enterprise data architecture, dimensional and semantic modeling, master data management, metadata, data quality, lineage, SQL, APIs, and ETL/ELT integration.
Cloud and BI technologies: Hands-on understanding of modern cloud data platforms and BI solutions; experience with Microsoft Fabric, Azure, Power BI, and related Microsoft data services is preferred.
Aviation data knowledge: Familiarity with maintenance and supply-chain data, including serialized components, aircraft configuration, maintenance planning, technical records, reliability, and inventory transactions.

Business leadership: Strong judgment connecting data investments to safety, operational readiness, contract delivery, customer commitments, and financial performance.
Communication: Ability to explain data limitations, security requirements, architectural decisions, and complex technical concepts to executives, operational leaders, technical specialists, and front-line users.
Program management: Proven ability to manage priorities, budgets, vendors, dependencies, risks, and organizational change in complex environments.
Collaboration: Strong influencing and relationship-building skills, with the ability to work effectively across multidisciplinary teams without relying solely on formal authority.

Chief Transformation Officer (CTO)Job Description Position:         Chief Transformation Officer (CTO) Reports to:  Chief Executive Officer (CEO)
Status:            Senior Leadership Position
Scope:            National transformation, digital platforms, innovation and modernisation

Position Purpose The Chief Transformation Officer (CTO) is a senior leadership role responsible for leading Lifesaving Society Canada’s transformation agenda and converting strategic priorities into sustainable national operating capabilities. The CTO will oversee VITA (CRM), artificial intelligence, the digital landscape and training manuals, virtual training, and related transformation initiatives. The position reports to the CEO, operates with significant delegated authority, manages related budgets and vendors, and works across the Board of Directors, Management Team, Branches, committees and external partners.
Leadership Mandate • Provide enterprise-wide leadership for LSC transformation initiatives, ensuring projects are coordinated, prioritized, resourced and aligned with LSC’s strategic direction, programs and delivery models.
•  Act independently within approved authority, escalating matters to the CEO or Board when they involve material strategic, financial, policy, privacy, security or reputational implications.
• Translate transformation strategy into clear roadmaps, implementation plans, governance structures, budgets, milestones, accountabilities and measurable outcomes.
•  Serve as a bridge between national strategy and practical implementation across the National Office and provincial Branches.

Key Accountabilities 1.  Transformation Strategy and Portfolio Leadership • Lead and coordinate LSC’s transformation portfolio, including VITA, AI, development, digital-resource modernization and virtual training.
• Establish integrated roadmaps, priorities, dependencies, milestones, risk controls and performance measures across transformation initiatives to include the subscription model.
• Identify opportunities to improve service delivery, operational efficiency, user experience, scalability, national consistency and revenue sustainability.
• Prepare recommendations, business cases and decision materials for the CEO, Management Team, Board and committees.
• Ensure transformation work reflects LSC’s national structure, Branch realities, program standards and delivery model.
2.  VITA (CRM) Platform Leadership • Provide national operational ownership and product coordination for VITA through implementation, stabilization and ongoing evolution.
• Manage the VITA scope baseline, roadmap, backlog, release calendar, gap register and national decision log.
• Lead the relationship with the platform developer/vendor and other service providers, including requirements clarification, delivery coordination, issue escalation, defect management, testing, acceptance criteria, service performance and documentation.
• Coordinate Branch readiness, migration, launch planning, hyper-care, training, issue triage, adoption monitoring and communication with Branch VITA Leads and Data Stewards.
• Maintain disciplined national change management for requests affecting shared data, workflows, permissions, reporting, integrations, configuration, scope and cross-Branch operations.
• Coordinate data governance and reporting, including data definitions, controlled values, data-quality measures, duplicate-management rules, reporting definitions and dashboard-access governance.
• Oversee VITA policies, business rules, user guides, role-based training materials, Branch toolkits, job aids, FAQs, release communications and other adoption resources.
• Ensure access and permissions are governed through an approved role-permission model, appropriate authorization, periodic review and segregation-of-duties controls; the CTO is accountable for business governance of access, not unrestricted technical control by a single individual.
• Coordinate privacy, security and compliance processes with the designated privacy/compliance resource and ensure risks are appropriately identified and escalated.
• Develop costed recommendations for post-implementation enhancements, support, staffing, funding and the long-term role of VITA in LSC’s digital architecture.
3.  Artificial Intelligence • Develop and lead an LSC approach to responsible AI adoption that supports operations, program delivery, service quality and organizational capacity.
• Identify, assess and prioritize practical AI use cases, including opportunities to streamline work, improve knowledge access and support decision-making.
• Establish appropriate governance, risk, privacy, security, human oversight and change-management practices for AI use.
• Build organizational AI literacy through guidance, training and practical support for staff and volunteers.
• Monitor emerging AI capabilities and recommend investments, pilots and policies appropriate to LSC.
5.  Digital Landscape and Training Resources • Lead the development of an integrated digital landscape for access to LSC resources and manuals.
• Oversee approaches to digital access, permissions, security, fees, version control and distribution of training and operational resources.
• Work with program leaders and Branches to ensure digital resources are current, accessible, practical and aligned with national standards.
• Identify opportunities to reduce duplication and improve the discoverability and management of national digital content.
6.  Virtual Training and Online Learning • Lead the development and expansion of virtual training and future online course offerings.
• Coordinate platform requirements, online registration, fee models, learner experience, training resources and operational support.
7.  Governance, Stakeholder and Change Leadership • Work   directly   with    the   CEO,  Board   of    Directors,   Management  Team,  Branches, commissions/committees and project groups on transformation priorities.
• Prepare clear reports, recommendations, dashboards, risk updates and decision materials for governance and management audiences.
• Maintain appropriate governance artifacts, including RACI/accountability frameworks, risk and issue registers, change logs, decision logs, policies, SOPs and project records.
• Lead organizational change, communications, training and adoption activities so that new systems and operating models are understood and used effectively.
• Build strong working relationships across LSC while respecting Branch operational responsibilities and national standards.
8.  Financial, Vendor and Resource Management • Develop and manage budgets for the transformation portfolio and its component initiatives.
• Monitor expenditures, forecasts, contracts and financial performance; identify variances and recommend corrective action.
• Lead procurement and vendor/service-provider relationships within delegated authority, with clear deliverables, service expectations and accountability.
• Assess resource and staffing requirements and recommend sustainable operating models for transformation functions.
• Ensure projects have realistic costs, timelines, ownership, risk controls and measures of success.

Qualifications and Experience • Progressive leadership experience in organizational transformation, digital modernization, technology-enabled service delivery, operations or a related field.
• Experience leading complex cross-functional initiatives involving multiple stakeholders, competing priorities and organizational change.
• Experience with CRM or enterprise platforms, vendor management, implementation, stabilization and continuous improvement.
• Experience developing and managing budgets, business cases, contracts and multi-year investment plans.
• Working knowledge of AI opportunities, governance and responsible adoption in an organizational setting.
• Experience working with senior management, boards, committees and governance processes.
• A relevant post-secondary credential or an equivalent combination of education and senior-level experience.
• Demonstrated knowledge of Lifesaving Society Canada, its programs, national/Branch delivery model and stakeholder environment is preferred.
• Knowledge of French, both written and spoken, is an asset.

Core Competencies • Strategic leadership: connects long-term direction to practical execution and measurable outcomes.
• Independent judgement: makes sound decisions within delegated authority and knows when escalation is required.
• Transformation leadership: leads people, process and technology change across complex stakeholder environments.
• Program and project leadership: manages interdependent initiatives, risks, timelines, resources and decisions.
• Relationship management: builds trust with the Board, Management Team, Branches, committees, vendors and partners.
• Financial acumen: develop budgets, evaluates investments and manages resources responsibly.
• Digital and data literacy: understands CRM, digital platforms, data governance, AI and online service delivery.
• Communication and change leadership: explains complex issues clearly and builds readiness, training and adoption.

Key Relationships • Internal: CEO; Board of Directors; Management Team; National Office staff; provincial Branches; commissions, committees and project teams.
• External: technology vendors and developers; consultants; service providers; training and digital partners; other stakeholders as assigned.

Initial Priorities • Assume leadership of the remaining VITA implementation, transition and stabilization work, with a structured handover from current project leadership.
• Confirm an integrated transformation roadmap, governance framework, budget and reporting cadence across VITA, AI, digital resources and virtual training.
• Establish clear decision rights, risk controls, vendor accountability and Branch engagement mechanisms for transformation initiatives.
• Develop practical recommendations for the long-term operating model and resource requirements
for LSC’s transformation portfolio.
